description: The ten cloud genera of the WMO International Cloud Atlas, with their étage, precipitation and typical characteristics.

source.title: WMO International Cloud Atlas (WMO-No. 407), Table 2: summary of the cloud classification
source.note: Names and classification follow Table 2. Étage heights follow the Atlas. Precipitation and characteristics are written for Architeuthis.

genera.name: Cirrus
genera.appearance: Detached white filaments, hooks or narrow bands of ice crystals, silky in sheen, casting no shadow.
genera.significance: Fair weather when isolated. Hooked or thickening Cirrus spreading across the sky often runs ahead of a warm front, 12 to 24 hours before rain.

genera.name: Cirrocumulus
genera.appearance: Thin white sheet or patch of very small grains or ripples without shading, each element less than 1 degree wide.
genera.significance: Short-lived and rarely widespread. Marks moisture and slight instability aloft, with no weather at sea level.

genera.name: Cirrostratus
genera.appearance: Transparent whitish veil, fibrous or smooth, covering part or all of the sky. Sun and Moon stay sharp and often show a halo.
genera.significance: A spreading and thickening veil usually announces a warm front or depression within about a day, with wind backing in the northern hemisphere.

genera.name: Altocumulus
genera.appearance: White or grey sheet or patches of rounded masses, rolls or lenses, usually with shading, each element 1 to 5 degrees wide.
genera.significance: Usually little weather: precipitation mostly evaporates as virga. Turreted Altocumulus (castellanus, floccus) on a morning foretells thunderstorms later in the day.

genera.name: Altostratus
genera.appearance: Greyish or bluish uniform sheet covering most of the sky, thin enough in places to show the Sun as through ground glass, without halo.
genera.significance: Thickening Altostratus follows Cirrostratus ahead of a warm front: rain usually starts within hours as it lowers into Nimbostratus.

genera.name: Nimbostratus
genera.appearance: Dark grey, thick and featureless layer that hides the Sun completely, often with ragged low cloud (pannus) beneath.
genera.significance: Steady rain or snow for hours, poor visibility and often strong wind, typical of warm fronts and the core of depressions.

genera.name: Stratocumulus
genera.appearance: Grey or whitish layer or patches of rounded masses and rolls, with dark parts, each element wider than 5 degrees.
genera.significance: The most common cloud over the oceans, capping a stable marine boundary layer. Grey skies and moderate wind, at most light rain or drizzle.

genera.name: Stratus
genera.appearance: Uniform grey layer with a very low base, often hiding high ground and masts, through which the Sun outline is clearly visible. Ragged shreds (fractus) under rain.
genera.significance: Forms in moist air cooled from below, as warm air flows over colder water: poor visibility and often fog where the base reaches the sea.

genera.name: Cumulus
genera.appearance: Detached dense clouds with sharp outlines, flat dark bases and brilliant white rising domes or towers.
genera.significance: Flat Cumulus (humilis) means fair weather and steady trade winds. Towering Cumulus (congestus) brings showers and gusts, and may grow into Cumulonimbus.

genera.name: Cumulonimbus
genera.appearance: Heavy dense tower reaching the high étage, with a dark ragged base and, when mature, a fibrous anvil (incus) of ice at its top.
genera.significance: Thunderstorm cloud: violent squalls and wind shifts under its arc cloud, heavy showers, hail, lightning and waterspouts.
